means: Eyes directed off-camera - the character is deliberately not meeting the viewer.
does: Breaks eye contact and turns the gaze out of frame. It is vaguer and weaker than its opposite because it names an absence instead of a direction: the model has to invent where 'away' is, and it invents inconsistently. Naming the direction lands far harder - looking down, looking to the side, downcast eyes, averted gaze - which is exactly what this project's emotion presets reach for. Treat looking away as a fallback for when the direction genuinely does not matter.
reach_for_it: evasion, shame and discomfort - and pair it with an actual direction unless you want the gaze to wander
used_in: the eyes field of emotions/cold.json and embarrassed.json. Note that shame, doubt and focus all deliberately use 'looking down' instead - the more specific tag wins
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short dark hair, plain jacket, standing, city street, daytime
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
